title: Three Januaries and One Short Bell
subtitle: 人际沟通 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）
meta: 主题语境：人际沟通（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·人际沟通与交流）　|　核心词汇：hello　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 hello 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the porter ① said the hello that no stranger in the courtyard would have described, and he said the saying was the whole of the January. The ② hello, meaning the greeting itself and not the bell, ran three Januarys and stayed undescribed in the book; a hello, he said, is the only thing in a courtyard that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ hello in that courtyard had the same short bell beside it, and the ④ hello at the far stair, meaning the nod they kept for the children to repeat and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A hello, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the porter said the describing is the part that fills three Januarys.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the hello was the whole of the matter, meaning the welcome and not the greeting. The ⑥ hello, meaning the welcome and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; hello, he said, is either something you say or the only word that means both a greeting and a welcome. He said the welcome is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ hello had become a line in a notebook, and the notebook had become an argument about the short bell. The ⑧ hello of the whole thing, the porter wrote in December, was one courtyard and three Januarys of describing; hello, he said, is either the nod at the far stair or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ hello I remember is the greeting described in the notebook, which closed in 1973 and is still described as the quietest in the courtyard. A ⑩ hello, my mother said in 1975, is the only greeting that improves by being described; every hello, she said, is a welcome that has agreed to look like a greeting. She said the welcome was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 问候；你好（指院子里每一声旁边的那一声）
B. n. 问候；你好（指那声问候语本身，与铃相对）
C. 固定搭配：say the hello 说一句你好
D. n. 问候；你好（指留给孩子们学说的一句那一声）
E. n. 问候之事（抽象总称，指一处院子的问候之事）
F. n. 问候；你好（指本子里写到、被记下的的那一声）
G. n. 欢迎、亲近（指一件事里人人都说却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 亲近（抽象总称，指人人都说却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: say the hello 意为“说一句你好”，1966 年那位门房把院子里没有一位陌生人肯描述的一声问候做了一遍。
hello 意为“问候；你好”，指那声问候语本身而不是铃，它经过了三个一月而在簿子上没有被描述。
hello 意为“问候；你好”，指院子里每一声旁边的那一声，每一声旁边都有同一只小小的短铃。
hello 意为“问候；你好”，指最远那处楼梯口留给孩子们学说的一句那一声，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
hello 意为“欢迎、亲近”，指一件事里人人都说却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份亲近就是那件事的全部。
hello 意为“亲近”，指人人都说却无人提起的那样东西而不是那声问候语，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
hello 意为“问候；你好”，指本子里写到、被记下的的那一声，到 1971 年这一声成了本子里的一行。
hello 意为“问候之事”，门房十二月写道，整件事的问候之事是一处院子和三个一月的描述。
hello 意为“问候；你好”，我记得的是本子里描述过的那一声，1973 年作别了，至今仍被说成院子里最安静的一声。
hello 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，问候是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的问候语。
